sets.title: Pie chart data: share of the total sales of ₹4,000 crore among six companies, and Bar chart data: number of employees (in hundreds)
Pie chart data: share of total rice production of 2,400 lakh tonnes among five states, and Bar chart data: area under cultivation (lakh hectares)
Pie chart data: share of 1,500 lakh passengers carried in a year by five railway zones, and Bar chart data: number of trains run (in hundreds)
Pie chart data: share of 3,000 runs scored by a team in a season among six batters, and Bar chart data: innings batted
Pie chart data: share of 2,000 units of electricity consumed (in million units) among five cities, and Bar chart data: population (in lakh)
Pie chart data: share of 1,200 crore units of FMCG packs sold, among five regional brands, and Bar chart data: number of distributors (in hundreds)

questions.questionText: What is the central angle of the sector for Chola Textiles in the pie chart?
questions.shortcut: 1% of the pie = 3.6°.

questions.questionText: What is the sales of Bharat Motors? (in ₹ crore)
questions.shortcut: Total × share ÷ 100.

questions.questionText: What is the average sales of the companies whose pie share is below 20%? (in ₹ crore)
questions.explanation: Entities below 20%: Chola Textiles (15%), Deccan Steel (10%), Falcon Paper (10%). Their total = 35% of 4000 = 1400; average = 1400 ÷ 3 = 466.7.
questions.shortcut: Strictly below 20% excludes entities at exactly 20%.

questions.questionText: Which company has the highest sales per unit of employees?
questions.explanation: Per unit: Aarav Foods 20.00, Bharat Motors 10.00, Chola Textiles 20.00, Deccan Steel 10.00, Eastern Pharma 32.00, Falcon Paper 25.00. Highest is Eastern Pharma.
questions.shortcut: Compare pie % ÷ bar value; the total is a common multiplier and can be ignored.

questions.questionText: Find the ratio of the sales per unit of employees of Eastern Pharma to that of Deccan Steel. (Give as a decimal correct to two decimal places.)
questions.shortcut: Ratio = (pie%₁ ÷ bar₁) ÷ (pie%₂ ÷ bar₂); the total cancels.

questions.questionText: By how much does the rice production of West Bengal exceed that of Tamil Nadu? (in lakh tonnes)
questions.shortcut: Subtract the percentages first, then take that % of the total.

questions.questionText: What is the central angle of the sector for Tamil Nadu in the pie chart?
questions.shortcut: 1% of the pie = 3.6°.

questions.questionText: Find the rice production per unit of area under cultivation for Punjab, in lakh tonnes per lakh hectare. (Correct to one decimal place.)
questions.shortcut: First convert the pie share into a value, then divide by the bar value.

questions.questionText: What is the average rice production of the states whose pie share is below 20%? (in lakh tonnes)
questions.explanation: Entities below 20%: Tamil Nadu (10%), Andhra Pradesh (15%). Their total = 25% of 2400 = 600; average = 600 ÷ 2 = 300.
questions.shortcut: Strictly below 20% excludes entities at exactly 20%.

questions.questionText: Suppose the rice production of Punjab rises by 50% while that of every other state stays the same. What percentage of the new total will Punjab then account for? (Correct to one decimal place.)
questions.shortcut: The total changes too; do not divide by the old total.

questions.questionText: What is the passengers carried of Southern? (in lakh)
questions.shortcut: Total × share ÷ 100.

questions.questionText: What is the central angle of the sector for Northern in the pie chart?
questions.shortcut: 1% of the pie = 3.6°.

questions.questionText: Which zone has the highest passengers carried per unit of trains run?
questions.explanation: Per unit: Southern 9.00, Western 3.75, Northern 7.50, Eastern 4.50, Central 6.00. Highest is Southern.
questions.shortcut: Compare pie % ÷ bar value; the total is a common multiplier and can be ignored.

questions.questionText: Find the passengers carried per unit of trains run for Central, in lakh passengers per hundred trains. (Correct to one decimal place.)
questions.shortcut: First convert the pie share into a value, then divide by the bar value.

questions.questionText: Find the ratio of the passengers carried per unit of trains run of Southern to that of Western. (Give as a decimal correct to two decimal places.)
questions.shortcut: Ratio = (pie%₁ ÷ bar₁) ÷ (pie%₂ ÷ bar₂); the total cancels.

questions.questionText: What is the central angle of the sector for Rohan in the pie chart?
questions.shortcut: 1% of the pie = 3.6°.

questions.questionText: Which batter has the highest runs scored per unit of innings batted?
questions.explanation: Per unit: Rohan 31.25, Siddharth 37.50, Tilak 45.00, Umesh 25.00, Vikram 24.00, Yash 37.50. Highest is Tilak.
questions.shortcut: Compare pie % ÷ bar value; the total is a common multiplier and can be ignored.

questions.questionText: Find the runs scored per unit of innings batted for Vikram, in runs per innings. (Correct to one decimal place.)
questions.shortcut: First convert the pie share into a value, then divide by the bar value.

questions.questionText: What is the average runs scored of the batters whose pie share is below 20%? (in runs)
questions.explanation: Entities below 20%: Tilak (15%), Umesh (10%), Yash (10%). Their total = 35% of 3000 = 1050; average = 1050 ÷ 3 = 350.
questions.shortcut: Strictly below 20% excludes entities at exactly 20%.

questions.questionText: Suppose the runs scored of Siddharth rises by 20% while that of every other batter stays the same. What percentage of the new total will Siddharth then account for? (Correct to one decimal place.)
questions.shortcut: The total changes too; do not divide by the old total.

questions.questionText: By how much does the electricity consumed of Salem exceed that of Tiruppur? (in million units)
questions.shortcut: Subtract the percentages first, then take that % of the total.

questions.questionText: What is the combined electricity consumed of all cities that have more than 15 lakh of population? (in million units)
questions.explanation: Entities with more than 15: Coimbatore (20%), Salem (30%). Total share = 50% of 2000 = 1000.
questions.shortcut: Add the qualifying pie percentages first, then convert once.

questions.questionText: Which city has the highest electricity consumed per unit of population?
questions.explanation: Per unit: Coimbatore 25.00, Madurai 20.00, Trichy 50.00, Salem 15.00, Tiruppur 25.00. Highest is Trichy.
questions.shortcut: Compare pie % ÷ bar value; the total is a common multiplier and can be ignored.

questions.questionText: Find the electricity consumed per unit of population for Coimbatore, in million units per lakh people. (Correct to one decimal place.)
questions.shortcut: First convert the pie share into a value, then divide by the bar value.

questions.questionText: Find the ratio of the electricity consumed per unit of population of Trichy to that of Salem. (Give as a decimal correct to two decimal places.)
questions.shortcut: Ratio = (pie%₁ ÷ bar₁) ÷ (pie%₂ ÷ bar₂); the total cancels.

questions.questionText: What is the packs sold of Malabar Mix? (in crore packs)

questions.questionText: What is the average packs sold of the brands whose pie share is below 20%? (in crore packs)
questions.explanation: Entities below 20%: Ooty Biscuits (15%), Malabar Mix (10%). Their total = 25% of 1200 = 300; average = 300 ÷ 2 = 150.
questions.shortcut: Strictly below 20% excludes entities at exactly 20%.

questions.questionText: What is the combined packs sold of all brands that have more than 16 hundreds of distributors of distributors? (in crore packs)
questions.explanation: Entities with more than 16: Pongal Foods (35%), Cauvery Chips (20%). Total share = 55% of 1200 = 660.
questions.shortcut: Add the qualifying pie percentages first, then convert once.

questions.questionText: Which brand has the highest packs sold per unit of distributors?
questions.explanation: Per unit: Kongu Snacks 15.00, Pongal Foods 15.00, Ooty Biscuits 15.00, Malabar Mix 24.00, Cauvery Chips 7.50. Highest is Malabar Mix.
questions.shortcut: Compare pie % ÷ bar value; the total is a common multiplier and can be ignored.

questions.questionText: Suppose the packs sold of Malabar Mix rises by 20% while that of every other brand stays the same. What percentage of the new total will Malabar Mix then account for? (Correct to one decimal place.)
